_comment: credential-inventory.v1.json — data for ops/credential-health.py (the daily credential-health lane wired into tools/health-check.py). One entry per credential CARR needs to run unattended. Adding a credential later is a config edit here, not a code change. NEVER put a secret VALUE in this file — same rule secrets-inventory.md states for itself. Built 2026-09-24 off Joe's survey: CARR is moving off interactive logins to long-lived scoped tokens, and this lane is what tells him before one lapses.
_probe_types: shell_exit_status (run `command`, exit code only, stdout/stderr discarded) | cloudflare_auth (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN env if set -> Cloudflare token-verify endpoint, HTTP status + expires_on field only; else falls back to shell_exit_status's `command` — retained for a machine that has not migrated off `wrangler login` yet) | cloudflare_token_file (reads token_key out of the dotenv-shaped file at `path`, mode-600-checked, never the wrangler fallback -> Cloudflare token-verify endpoint, HTTP status + result.status + result.expires_on only) | claude_cli_token_age (reads token_key out of the dotenv-shaped file at `path`, checks length/prefix shape, runs `claude -p "Reply with exactly: PONG" --max-turns 1` from a throwaway cwd with ONLY that one env var set and scans only for the word PONG, and ages the token from a first-seen mint date this lane records itself in out/credential-health-mint-state.json — never the token value) | neon_api (reads token_key out of the dotenv-shaped file at `path` if configured and present, else NEON_API_KEY env -> GET /api_keys on Neon's API — the same path tools/rotate-credential.py verifies a rotated key with — HTTP status only; 401/403 is failed, any other non-2xx is unknown with the status in the detail) | worker_bearer_health (reads token_key out of the dotenv-shaped file at `path` if configured and present, else the token_env env var -> POST tools/list against the deployed Worker's /mcp; ok requires BOTH HTTP 200 and a JSON-RPC `result` key in the body, never anything inside it) | file_presence_age (local file's existence + mtime age, never its contents) | config_only (no live probe; status comes entirely from the `expiry` block below, which Joe edits by hand)

credentials.name: cloudflare-deploy-token
credentials.replacement_plan: Already the long-lived scoped replacement for the retired interactive `wrangler login` OAuth grant. If this probe fails, mint a fresh scoped token in the Cloudflare dashboard (Workers Scripts:Edit + Account Settings:Read on the CARR account only), paste it into ~/.config/carr/tokens.env as CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=<value>, and `chmod 600` the file. If the finding is insecure_file_permissions rather than the token itself, `chmod 600 ~/.config/carr/tokens.env` is the whole fix — the token does not need to be rotated for that alone.

credentials.name: claude-cli-oauth-token-studio
credentials.display_name: Claude Code CLI long-lived login (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, Studio)
credentials.replacement_plan: Already the long-lived scoped replacement for the interactive Claude Code CLI login, minted by `claude setup-token` (2026-09-24, ~1 year validity). If this probe fails or reports expiring_soon, run `claude setup-token` again, paste the new value into ~/.config/carr/tokens.env as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=<value>, and confirm the file stays mode 600. A rotated token resets this lane's own age tracking on its next run (it re-records today as the mint date the first time it sees the new value's fingerprint).
credentials.doc_pointer: CLAUDE.md — Dell migration trigger section (Claude-only launch machine)

credentials.name: neon-api-key
credentials.replacement_plan: Already a long-lived scoped key (control-plane read, per secrets-inventory.md). Rotate it in the Neon console if this probe fails and re-paste into db.env by hand; no agent holds the value.

credentials.name: carr-mcp-probe-token
credentials.replacement_plan: Server-issued bearer, already long-lived and scoped to the locked 'probe' profile (mcp-server/src/mcp.js). If it fails, Joe re-mints it with `wrangler secret put PROBE_TOKENS` per the runbook in mcp-server/smoke-reads.sh's header and re-pastes the matching value into mcp-tokens.env; no agent ever holds it.

credentials.name: carr-mcp-local-token
credentials.replacement_plan: Server-issued bearer, already long-lived, one per machine (joe-local / dell-local). If it fails, Joe re-mints via `wrangler secret put LOCAL_TOKENS` per pipelines/provision-local-client.sql and re-pastes the matching value on the affected machine; no agent ever holds it.

credentials.name: gh-cli-auth
credentials.replacement_plan: Replace with a fine-grained personal access token (repo-scoped to jbookout/carr-system, no org-wide grant), stored the same way as any other CARR token and rotated on the date Joe sets below once he creates it.

expiry._note: Joe sets configured_rotation_date (YYYY-MM-DD) here once the fine-grained PAT exists and carries an expiry; null means no configured window and the probe result stands on its own.

credentials.name: claude-cli-studio
credentials.replacement_plan: Replace interactive login with `claude setup-token` (a long-lived scoped token) so an unattended run never hits an interactive auth prompt.
credentials.doc_pointer: CLAUDE.md — Dell migration trigger section (Claude-only launch machine)

credentials.name: claude-cli-macbook
credentials.replacement_plan: Replace interactive login with `claude setup-token` (a long-lived scoped token) so an unattended run never hits an interactive auth prompt. Only meaningful when this lane runs ON the MacBook — probed from the Studio it can only ever read the Studio's own keychain entry of the same service name.
credentials.doc_pointer: CLAUDE.md — Dell migration trigger section (Claude-only launch machine)

credentials.name: codex-cli-auth-studio
credentials.replacement_plan: The complete absence of ~/.codex is an expected supported state on a Claude-only launch machine (CLAUDE.md, Dell migration trigger) — this row reports `unknown` there, never `failed`. Where Codex is in use, replace with whatever long-lived token Codex's own CLI issues in place of interactive ChatGPT-token auth, once one exists.

credentials.name: codex-cli-auth-macbook
credentials.replacement_plan: Same as the Studio row. Only meaningful when this lane runs ON the MacBook — probed from the Studio it reads the Studio's own filesystem, not the MacBook's.

credentials.name: google-oauth-worker-client
credentials.location: Worker secret (wrangler); OAuth client in Google Cloud project carr-record-layer
credentials.replacement_plan: No local probe is possible — Joe holds this credential and no agent ever has (secrets-inventory.md). If the Google Cloud consent screen is still in 'testing' publishing status, Google expires the refresh token after 7 days; the fix is Joe publishing the consent screen (removes the 7-day cap) or re-consenting within the window. Set `expiry.google_testing_mode` true and `expiry.consent_screen_last_verified` to today whenever Joe re-verifies, so this row can compute the live window.

expiry._note: Joe sets google_testing_mode (true/false) and consent_screen_last_verified (YYYY-MM-DD, the date he last confirmed the consent screen state) by hand. Both null means 'not yet configured' and the row reports unknown rather than guessing.
